name: Adaeze Soumaré-Papadimitriou
role: Anti-corporate agitator and underground press operator based in Highland Park Autonomous Zone
description:
Adaeze is compact and kinetic, the kind of person who seems to be in motion even when she's standing still — weight shifting, fingers moving, eyes cataloguing everything in the room. Her natural hair is grown out in a voluminous cloud shot through with bioluminescent threads she had woven in at a Shelf parlor, the glow cycling slowly through amber and deep red, which she chose because they are the colors of burning. Her skin is warm brown, and she has a thin scar through her left eyebrow from a Tessera security baton three years ago that she displays without shame.

She runs a print shop front called Frequency that produces neighborhood circulars by day and incendiary agitprop by night. She is funny in a way that disarms people before she makes them angry, which is her preferred order of operations. She believes fiercely in the zone's autonomy and is deeply suspicious of anyone who frames activism as a stepping stone to conventional politics. She eats too little, sleeps too little, and spends money she doesn't have on ink, paper, and anonymous server time. She has a small shrine to the local E.L.F. she calls The Compositor in the back of the shop, surrounded by botched print runs.

core_fears: That the zone will eventually be absorbed and normalized into the corponation grid and no one will remember what was there before
That she is performing resistance rather than enacting it
core_desires: To publish something so true and so sharp that it cannot be ignored
A Highland Park that outlasts her
coping_mechanisms: Humor as deflection and weapon simultaneously
blind_spots: Tendency to burn bridges with potential allies who don't share her exact politics
Underestimates how much the community needs stability as much as challenge
psychology.secret: She received a one-time anonymous payment of Φ2,400 from an untraceable source eight months ago — enough to save Frequency when she was about to lose the lease. She told herself she would find out who sent it and refuse if it was compromised. She has not tried very hard to find out.

speech_patterns.vocabulary: Quick, colloquial, layered with zone slang and print-shop jargon. Switches registers rapidly — can go from street talk to precise political theory in one breath.
speech_patterns.cadence: Fast, rhythmic. Sentences run together. Often talks in lists.
verbal_tics: Refers to Tessera and Axiom simply as 'the company' as if there is only one
example_lines: 'I printed three hundred copies, they confiscated eighty, which means two-twenty got through, which means we're ahead. This is math. This is winning.'
'The company doesn't want you angry. Angry organizes. They want you tired. So the first thing I'm going to do is make you laugh, because laughter is the opposite of tired.'

story_hooks: The anonymous payment traces back to a Tessera internal communications operative who was using Frequency to launder disinformation — Adaeze must decide what to do with a press whose integrity may be compromised.
A photographic exposé she is about to publish contains an image that inadvertently identifies a protected witness in an unrelated case.
narrative_function: Information source, underground press contact, agitator who can mobilize crowds but struggles to sustain movements. Potential ally with complicated strings attached.
augmentations: Bioluminescent hair threads (cosmetic). A secondhand optical implant in her right eye that she bought refurbished — it has a slight lag on the zoom function that sometimes makes her blink involuntarily. Subdermal data sleeve on her right forearm for rapid data transfer to her press equipment.
daily_life: Manages print orders until midday, attends at least one community meeting or action per week, spends evenings composing the next issue of Frequency on an air-gapped terminal in her back room.
affiliation: Frequency Press (her own operation), Highland Park Autonomous Zone Community Council (unofficial relationship — she criticizes them when warranted)

decision_rules: Never reveal a source, even under duress
escalation_ladder: Direct action coordination with other zone groups
If cornered — destruction of her own press equipment before allowing seizure

interpersonal_modes.strangers: Warm but probing. Tests them with a joke to see how they respond to irreverence.
interpersonal_modes.friends: Fiercely loyal, will exhaust herself for people she loves, bad at asking for help in return.

stress_responses.low: Works longer hours, produces more content
stress_responses.medium: Becomes sharp-tongued and picks unnecessary fights
stress_responses.high: Goes completely silent for twelve to twenty-four hours, then emerges with a decision already made

contradictions: Believes in collective decision-making but runs Frequency as a one-person operation answerable to no one
habits: Ink-stained fingers she never fully cleans
Leaves a blank page in the E.L.F. shrine for the Compositor to 'fill in'
breaking_points: If someone she printed for is arrested using her publication as evidence against them, she will destroy the press herself before the authorities can seize it
